title: A pathway to improve Nb$_3$Sn for SRF accelerator cavities via Zr inclusion
summary: Nb$_3$Sn has the potential to exceed the performance of niobium-based superconducting radio-frequency (SRF) cavities, both in particle accelerators and in high-$Q_0$ cavities operating in multi-tesla magnetic fields for axion dark matter searches. We studied how the incorporation of Zr into the Nb$_3$Sn matrix by co-sputtering affects the microstructure and superconducting properties of Nb$_3$Sn films. As the atomic fraction of Zr increased, the surface morphology improved and the bulk and surface void densities decreased. At the optimal Zr content, the superconducting properties improved and a thinner surface niobium oxide formed. These results identify co-sputtered Nb$_3$Sn:Zr as a promising material to advance the performance limits of SRF cavities.

title: Coulomb Crystallization in Free Electron Beams
summary: Classical Coulomb crystals and quantum Wigner crystals typically arise when repulsive interactions order like-charged particles in spatially confined environments. Here, we show that transient crystallization can also emerge in freely propagating electron pulses without external trapping. Experimentally, we use a transmission electron microscope to measure number-resolved energy correlations in photoemitted pulses containing up to nine electrons, revealing strong correlations at small particle numbers that progressively disappear in the pulse interior as the number increases. To explain these observations, we combine many-body simulations with a one-dimensional statistical-mechanical model, showing that the leading and trailing electrons generate a self-induced longitudinal potential that transiently confines the inner particles, enabling the formation of an ordered chain during propagation. The resulting crystallization phase diagram reveals how many-body ordering dynamics can be understood in terms of evolving macroscopic beam properties, namely its geometry and the ratio of the mean Coulomb interaction energy to the longitudinal thermal energy. Extending this framework, we theoretically demonstrate that weak transverse guiding through electrostatic or optical ponderomotive forces can sustain crystallization at larger particle numbers and predict spontaneous longitudinal periodic bunching in continuous electron beams. Our results identify conditions under which stochastic Coulomb interactions can be harnessed to generate self-structured, strongly correlated electron beams in both pulsed and continuous regimes.

title: Subpercent accuracy in molecular electric quadrupole coupling: nuclear-size and relativistic effects in RaF
summary: We report a benchmark study of the electric-quadrupole hyperfine interaction in the electronic ground state of the RaF molecule, including finite-nuclear-size effects. The calculations include relativistic effects using the Dirac-Coulomb-Breit Hamiltonian and electron correlation up to perturbative quadruple excitations within the coupled cluster framework. At the achieved level of accuracy, penetration of the electronic density into the finite nuclear quadrupole distribution produces a non-negligible correction to the usual electric field gradient (EFG) description at the center of the nucleus and must be considered. At a fixed rms charge radius, the EFG is much less sensitive to the shape of the monopole nuclear charge distribution: electron wavefunctions computed using the Gaussian and Fermi nuclear charge models yield nearly identical EFGs. The recommended effective EFG parameter for the $X\,{}^{2}Σ_{1/2}$ electronic ground state is $\langle q\rangle_0=-5.178(21)$ a.u., with an estimated uncertainty reduced by an order of magnitude compared to previous studies. Combined with future measurements of electric-quadrupole hyperfine coupling constants in RaF, this result can be used to determine the nuclear quadrupole moments of Ra isotopes with record precision.

title: Parity-doublet spin interactions in ultracold polyatomic molecules
summary: Precision measurements exploit internal molecular structure to search for physics beyond the Standard Model. Reaching the entanglement-enhanced regime requires preparing and preserving correlated molecular states within the same manifold used for sensing. Parity-doublet states are central to proposals for precision measurements with polyatomic molecules because they enable large molecular polarization for enhanced sensitivity, and provide internal state co-magnetometry to suppress systematic errors. Here we report the observation and control of resonant dipolar exchange interactions in a parity-doublet sensing manifold of ultracold polyatomic molecules. Using laser-cooled CaOH molecules in a crossed optical dipole trap, we encode a pseudospin in the $\ell$-type parity-doublet states and observe two complementary signatures of interactions: a density-dependent Ramsey contrast decay and a spin-projection-dependent mean-field precession whose sign reverses with the initialized population imbalance. Both observables are well described by a common discrete truncated Wigner model using independently calibrated experimental parameters. We further Floquet-engineer the interaction anisotropy and observe suppressed many-body dephasing near the SU(2)-symmetric Heisenberg point, identifying a protected regime relevant for spin squeezing and precision measurement with dense molecular ensembles. Our results establish parity doublets as a coherent, interacting, and programmable molecular degree of freedom, connecting the polyatomic precision-measurement platform to dipolar many-body physics and opening a route to entanglement-enhanced tests of fundamental physics.

title: Derivation of OH sum rules without Rayleigh--Jeans approximation: a powerful tool for measuring the variation of fundamental physical constants
summary: In this paper, we show that the optical depths of any OH $Λ$-doublet quartet obey one exact linear relation in every velocity channel. No approximation is needed. The only exception is the $^{2}Π_{1/2}$ $J{=}1/2$ level, which has three transitions only, because its $F{=}0{\leftrightarrow}0$ line is strictly forbidden. The relation is $τ_{S_1}(v)/μ_{S_1}^{2}+τ_{S_2}(v)/μ_{S_2}^{2}=τ_{M_1}(v)/(aμ_{M_1}^{2})+τ_{M_2}(v)/(bμ_{M_2}^{2})$, where $a=2J^{2}+J-1$, $b=2J^{2}+3J$, and the $μ_i^{2}$ are reduced transition dipole moments derived from the catalogued Einstein $A$ coefficients. It holds equally for gas in local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE), for non-LTE gas, for masers and for conjugate gas. We suggest that it is a powerful tool for measuring the variation of fundamental physical constants.

title: Mediated Interactions between Fermi Polarons in the Strongly Interacting Regime
summary: Mediated interactions between quasiparticles lie at the heart of Landau Fermi-liquid theory, yet their behavior in the strongly correlated regime is not fully understood. Motivated by recent experiments [Nat. Phys. 20, 68--73 (2024)], we investigate mediated interactions between quasiparticles emerging from a Fermi sea---Fermi polarons---using zero-temperature quantum Monte Carlo methods. Our main result is that the Landau interaction between polarons remains repulsive in the strongly interacting regime for any coupling strength in the polaronic branch, in contrast to the downward trend observed experimentally near resonance. Deep in the short-range universal regime, our results are insensitive to the microscopic details of the interaction potential, providing robust evidence for the sign of the ground-state induced interaction. In addition, we determine the real-space interaction between static impurities, recovering a Ruderman-Kittel-Kasuya-Yosida (RKKY)-like behavior at weak coupling and the nonperturbative Born-Oppenheimer result at strong coupling. More broadly, our results establish a microscopic benchmark for how Landau quasiparticle interactions survive beyond the perturbative regime of strongly correlated quantum matter.

title: Experimental evidence for quantum Brownian motion in electron-metal decoherence
summary: Feynman once remarked that the double-slit experiment has in its heart the only mystery of quantum mechanics. Arguably, the scientific significance of double-slit experiments lies in motional decoherence and the mechanism behind it. Decoherence of motional states underpins our understanding of quantum-to-classical transition. It is also central to the operation of miniaturized quantum electron devices and poses a resolution limit for electron microscopes. In this work, we provide experimental evidence for the critical role of quantum Brownian motion in electron motional decoherence. We demonstrate, for the first time, clear signatures of electron-metal decoherence and its continuous tunability. Our experiment concludes a two-decade long search for experimental realization of the Anglin-Paz-Zurek proposal, establishing electron-microchannel systems as viable open quantum platforms for free-electron quantum optics. The quantitative agreement between experiment and theory further paves the way for testing the Caldeira-Leggett quantum dissipation theory with free electrons.

title: Controlled Dark-State Energy Storage and Work Extraction in V-Type Quantum Batteries
summary: The performance of a quantum battery depends not only on its ability to retain stored energy against unwanted discharge but also on the amount of useful work that can be extracted from it. Here, we investigate these complementary aspects in an ensemble of V-type qutrits coupled to a lossy cavity. By applying a finite splitting pulse to the two excited states of each qutrit, cavity-bright excitations are converted into atomic dark states, whose populations remain protected upon restoring degeneracy, even while the light-matter coupling remains active. Simulations with finite-duration pulses reveal a capture window governed by the competition among energy transfer, bright-to-dark conversion, and photon leakage. We further show that if the energy is stored in the fully symmetric atomic subspace, the passive energy is bounded by twice the transition energy for number of atoms $N\geq2$. Consequently, if the stored energy scales extensively with $N$, the ratio of extractable work to stored energy approaches unity in the thermodynamic limit. Comparing different initial preparations at equal mean input energy, we find that coherent-state can yield greater finite-time ergotropy despite capturing less energy, whereas Fock-state favors greater extractable work in the stationary component. Our results demonstrate how controlled dark-state population trapping in an atom-cavity coupled system can protect stored energy while providing a conditional route toward high extractable work.

title: Kinetic Slush in Dissipative Rydberg Arrays
summary: We investigate the nonequilibrium dynamics of a kinetic slush state realized via facilitated excitations in a two-dimensional dissipative Rydberg atom array. Utilizing kinetic Monte Carlo simulations in the strong dephasing regime, we show that tuning the laser detuning to compensate for nearest-neighbor interactions enables facilitated dynamics, while residual next-nearest-neighbor interactions induce kinetic frustration. This competition gives rise to an emergent slush phase characterized by pronounced dynamical heterogeneity and the coexistence of liquid- and solid-like configurations. By probing its nonequilibrium real-time evolution, we uncover a dynamical crossover from isotropic spreading to one-dimensional constrained growth, which can be continuously tuned by the frustration strength. Within this crossover regime, the slush dynamics generate fractal cluster geometries and generalized Ornstein-Zernike spatial correlations. Finite-size scaling analysis supports the system's proximity to criticality. Our findings establish driven-dissipative Rydberg systems as a highly controllable platform for engineering complex nonequilibrium soft-matter phenomena.

title: Fast diagonalization for matrix-free inversion of the nodal even-parity operator in hybrid finite element SPN transport
summary: The hybrid finite element method stores a dense inverse of the nodal even-parity operator for every node and energy group, and that storage limits the spatial and angular expansion orders, more tightly still on a GPU, whose memory is smaller than that of a host. This work introduces fast diagonalization for the nodal even-parity operator of the hybrid finite element SPN method: the stored dense inverse is replaced by the eigendecompositions of a planar, an axial and an angular factor, and the inverse is applied without being formed explicitly. Every even-parity moment of the SPN equations obeys an equation of the same diffusion form, with no mixed derivatives, so the angular coupling is the same in every spatial direction. On a node extruded along the axis, the operator is then an exact Kronecker sum of the three factors. The factorization merely recasts the computation, so the discretization and the solution are unchanged, and the nodes are not required to be identical to one another. The method is implemented for CPU and GPU hardware and compared with the dense inverse within one solver. On a pressurized water reactor core in SP3, the two paths agree to within round-off error, the storage falls from 3.76 GB to 821 kB, and the calculation is 4.15 times faster. On a 33-group fast reactor core, the dense inverse would occupy 24.9 GB and the dense path would need more memory than both the device and the host provide, whereas the factors occupy only 1.26 MB, so the solution can be obtained. The factorization thus reduces the storage of the nodal inverse by more than three orders of magnitude and brings multigroup core calculations at their required spatial expansion orders within the memory of a single GPU.

title: QMOMKit: A C++ library for quadrature-based moment methods
summary: QMOMKit is an open-source C++ library for the phase-space evolution of population balance equations with quadrature-based moment methods. The present version implements the quadrature method of moments (QMOM) and the conditional quadrature method of moments (CQMOM). QMOMKit is designed to be independent of any particular application and can be used either as a standalone solver for spatially homogeneous population models or as a local phase-space solver coupled to a host application. It handles the numerical aspects of the evolution of a population in phase space, including quadrature reconstruction, advection of the quadrature abscissas, and changes to the population through moment sources and phase-space boundary contributions. The number of quadrature nodes is adapted to what the supplied moments support, subject to prescribed bounds of the phase-space coordinates, and the CQMOM implementation supports an arbitrary number of phase-space dimensions as well as any conditioning order. The principal numerical algorithms of QMOMKit are verified against analytical and manufactured solutions. Standalone spatially homogeneous applications, ranging from aerosol evaporation to particle dynamics and fragmentation, are compared with Monte Carlo solutions of the same population models, while coupling examples with OpenFOAM and deal.II demonstrate how QMOMKit can be embedded in finite-volume and discontinuous-Galerkin simulation frameworks. Together, these capabilities provide a tested and reusable foundation for a wide range of population-balance problems, and a basis for extending QMOMKit to other quadrature-based moment methods.

title: Efficient regime boundary detection in discontinuous simulation models
summary: Many computational models exhibit multiple operating regimes separated by abrupt or non-smooth transitions as the input parameters vary. Such regime transitions complicate the construction of global parametric reduced-order models, often necessitating large training datasets to capture the distinct system behaviors. Accurate regime boundary detection instead enables localized modeling strategies by partitioning the parameter space into regions of qualitatively distinct behavior. In many cases, regime switching corresponds to the excursion set of a simulator output. When such a quantity is discontinuous or non-smooth, regression-based algorithms for level set estimation can struggle to correctly approximate the boundary. In this work, we show that solving a resulting binary classification problem can improve sample efficiency and we further propose a novel adaptive sampling strategy for support vector machines. Unlike uncertainty-based sampling schemes, the proposed approach uses a continuous search space and efficiently explores the currently estimated boundary in its tangential directions by gradient-based dynamic sampling. Because the decision function admits analytical gradients, this exploration incurs negligible computational overhead relative to the underlying model evaluations. Then, a space-filling subset of the generated samples is selected as the next batch to be queried. We demonstrate improved sample efficiency compared to existing active learning algorithms on analytical and numerical examples. The proposed method provides a sample-efficient framework for regime boundary detection in a broad class of discontinuous simulation-driven problems.

title: Continuum thermodynamics of chemically reacting multi-temperature fluid mixtures
summary: We develop a continuum-thermodynamic model for chemically reacting, multi-velocity and multi-temperature fluid mixtures. Partial balances of mass, momentum and total energy are closed using a single entropy density depending jointly on the constituent mass and nonkinetic internal-energy densities. Its partial derivatives determine the constituent temperatures and chemical potentials. For the chosen entropy flux and separately treated volume deformation, the strengthened entropy principle yields a weighted Euler relation constraining the partial thermodynamic pressures. We construct thermodynamically consistent constitutive relations for viscosity, heat conduction, Maxwell--Stefan momentum exchange, thermal relaxation and nonlinear reaction kinetics. The baseline model includes thermo-diffusion and its reciprocal coupling; a fully coupled reciprocal completion is given within the stated isotropic co-factor class. An alternative formulation couples chemical conversion and energy redistribution through specified elementary processes. We identify the material functions required for closure and admissible shifts of constituent energy zeros. An ionization network with resolved electronic levels yields Saha-type ionization relations and Boltzmann excitation ratios under the stated detailed-balance assumptions, recovering the Saha--Eggert relation at common temperature. Competing electron- and heavy-particle processes can maintain stationary populations while transferring energy between groups at different prescribed temperatures.

title: Evaluation of upper-scale mechanical parameters of particulate aluminum-based nanocomposites from molecular simulations
summary: This paper focuses on the numerical and analytical determination of the mechanical parameters of aluminum-matrix nanocomposites using atomistic-scale simulations within a multiscale modeling framework. Molecular statics simulations were employed to evaluate the tensile and compressive behavior of Al based composites reinforced with nanosized alumina particles. Two classes of atomistic models were investigated. First, a unit-cell model containing a single Al2O3 monocrystal embedded in an aluminum matrix was used to examine the influence of the volume fraction of the ceramic inclusion on the effective mechanical properties. Second, a polycrystalline RVE model comprising an alumina particle was analyzed to assess the effect of the number of Al grains on effective properties. For each case, the mechanical response was characterized by stress-strain curves, enabling the identification of upper-scale material parameters associated with the elastic regime (bulk, shear and Young's modulus) and the damage stage (ultimate strength, ultimate strain, and failure strain). The isotropized elastic constants evaluated from molecular simulations were compared with classical Voigt-Reuss-Hill bounds to assess their applicability in the elastic regime. Finally, atomistic-scale simulation outputs provided insight into the dominant deformation/damage mechanisms (brittle versus ductile) and fracture modes (transgranular versus intergranular).

title: A Systematic Assessment of Artificial Flame Thickening for Thermodiffusively Unstable Lean Hydrogen Flames in Homogeneous Isotropic Turbulence
summary: The Artificially Thickened Flame (ATF) approach is widely used to render premixed flames resolvable on coarse computational meshes, but thickening alters their interaction with turbulence. While considerable research has focused on the effects of thickening on turbulence-induced flame wrinkling, its influence on the mean local flame propagation speed in turbulent, thermodiffusively unstable hydrogen flames remains poorly understood. More than 200 flame-resolved simulations of premixed flames in homogeneous isotropic turbulence with detailed chemistry and transport are used to systematically isolate and quantify the effects of artificial thickening. Thickening the flame by a factor $F$ increases its effective flame-scale Karlovitz number according to $Ka_{\mathrm{f}}^F = Ka_{\mathrm{f}}\sqrt{F}$, while decreasing its effective Damköhler number according to $Da_{\mathrm{f}}^F = Da_{\mathrm{f}}/F$. In the regime considered here, the former enhances the mean local flame speed, whereas the latter reduces flame wrinkling, resulting in opposing effects on the flame consumption speed; hence, changes in both local flame propagation and flame area must be accounted for. Simulations matched with respect to $Ka_{\mathrm{f}}^F$ and $Da_{\mathrm{f}}^F$ collapse across different thickening factors $F$ until the thickened flame approaches the integral or geometric length scales of the configuration. Based on these scaling relations, a self-consistent efficiency correction is proposed to recover the unthickened flame consumption speed. Since the efficiency factor feeds back on the effective Karlovitz and Damköhler numbers, it must be determined implicitly.

title: Walk on Multiscale Media: Compiling Editable and Composable Transport Medium Prefabs for Monte Carlo PDE Solvers
summary: Monte Carlo PDE solvers enable mesh-free pointwise queries, but repeatedly traversing heterogeneous media is costly, particularly in scenes with reusable or dynamically changing materials. We introduce Walk on Multiscale Media (WoMM), which compiles fine-scale transport into reusable, editable and composable transport prefabs. A probabilistic interpretation of multiscale finite-element bases and condensed operators yields coarse transitions retaining fine-scale material effects. Each prefab combines port-level operators, entrance-dependent exit distributions, and Poisson-marked trajectory records, enabling incremental updates for overlapping absorption fields, gradient-field steering through path reweighting and transient diffusion. Integrated with conventional Walk-on-Spheres in a hybrid continuous--discrete solver, these prefabs accelerate repeated pointwise PDE queries and support interactive material edits without repeatedly solving the fine-scale problem.

title: Development and assessment of a target-$ω$ interfacial turbulence-damping model for stratified gas--liquid flow
summary: Interfacial turbulence damping is required in Reynolds-averaged simulations of stratified gas--liquid flows when strong interfacial velocity gradients are present. In this work, we develop a target-$ω$ interfacial damping formulation for the low-Reynolds-number Wilcox-type $k$--$ω$ model in a one-field RANS/VOF framework. A gas-side target value of the specific dissipation rate $ω$ is constructed from an effective interfacial wall coordinate determined from the local resolved flow. The constructed target-$ω$ provides a smooth transition between the viscous and logarithmic limits through power-law blending and requires no calibration of model constants against target data. \textcolor{black}{The formulation is first assessed against three gas-layer DNS cases at $Re_τ\simeq180$ with different interface velocities. The model reproduces the principal features of the mean velocity, turbulent kinetic energy and Reynolds shear-stress distributions, while showing substantially weaker sensitivity to the near-interface grid resolution than the Egorov-type formulation, although some grid dependence remains on the coarsest mesh. The assessment is then extended to the co-current Fabre stratified-flow experiment at a higher Reynolds number and to the counter-current Stäbler experiment}. In both cases, the present formulation provides generally good predictions of the gas-side mean flow and turbulence statistics without case-specific adjustment. For the Stäbler case, in which the liquid level develops as part of the coupled two-phase solution, the predicted mean liquid depth agrees closely with the measured value. These results indicate that the target-$ω$ formulation provides a consistent interfacial turbulence-damping treatment for resolved large gas--liquid interfaces over the range of conditions considered.

title: Attention as Lattice Gauge Theory: Relations Interact Only Through Wilson Loops
comment: 7 pages, 1 figure. Accepted at the 9th Workshop on Machine Learning and the Physical Sciences (ML4PS 2026), co-located with NeurIPS 2026
summary: Relations compose through the entity they share - Alice is Bob's mother and Bob is Carol's father, so Alice is Carol's grandmother - and the order matters, since a father's mother is not a mother's father; verifying a composed relation means closing the loop. We show that if each entity's coordinate frame may be rotated independently (per-entity frame freedom), three things follow. In the pure-gauge sector, relations that share no cycle cannot interact at all. The only gauge-invariant score of a triangle is a class function of its holonomy $H = T_{ij} T_{jk} T_{ki}$ - a Wilson loop. And the only equivariant update of an edge is $U = Ψ(H)\, T_{ij}$ with $Ψ$ conjugation-equivariant. Edge attention by Wilson loops is therefore not one design among many but the unique form the symmetry permits. Three communities hold pieces of this form: the commuting-operator embeddings of knowledge graphs are its abelian (commuting) sector; AlphaFold's triangle update and the Edge Transformer have its shape - an edge updated through the third vertex - without its constraints; and lattice QCD builds it equivariantly on lattices. We instantiate the equivariant sub-family on general relational graphs as holonomy attention. With no training and composition alone, it infers unobserved $S_4$ relations on sparse graphs at 0.88 with a fifth of the edges corrupted, at or slightly below specialist synchronization algorithms, where every commutative architecture is capped at 0.083; its holonomy score flags corrupted triangles at AUC 0.99 where commuting scores are capped at 0.76 by a second selection rule, and it separates clusters without labels.

title: Spatial Colorimetric Mapping of pH and Dissolved Carbon during Convective Dissolution of CO{\_2}: Constraints from Domain, Geometry, and Indicator Mix on Measurement Reliability
summary: Quantifying the dissolution and buoyancy-driven transport of CO2-rich water is critical to understanding solubility trapping mechanism in geologic storage. Analog-fluid density driven convection experiments do not represent CO2 dissolution chemistry or the aqueous CO2 density-concentration monotonic relationship. X-ray tomography does not provide enough contrast to directly measure dissolved CO2. Spatial colorimetry provides an inexpensive method to map pH and estimate total dissolved inorganic carbon (CT) via carbonate equilibrium assumptions. However, the effects of experimental conditions such as domain (free fluid and porous), geometry (2D and 3D), and indicator mix concentration on the reliability of pH and CT measurements remain unexplored. We evaluated how these factors affect the reliability of measurements using two different colorimetric models (hue and spherical coordinates (θ and φ)). Hue was reliable in all domains whereas θ-φ was reliable in free fluid. Lower indicator mix concentration increased the chromatic sensitivity at low pH in free fluid; however, it did not produce sufficient color contrast for pH calibration and mapping in the porous domain. In the porous domain, θ-φ calibration was 33 times more susceptible to noise than hue. Temporal pH noise was less than 0.01 units; spatial noise changed domain-mean CT by 0.6-4.4{\%}. Both models were able to resolve CO2-rich plumes in free fluid; however, θ-φ had sharper plume boundaries than hue. The temporal evolution of CO2 dissolution resolved by the color models agreed more in 2D than 3D. These findings provide a reliability framework for studying subsurface dissolution and mixing of CO2.

title: Catastrophes in Reconnections of Optical Vortex Rings
summary: A small change in parameters leads to a small change in the outcomes, in most cases. For instance, an optical vortex ring, created in the superposition of two laser beams, can slightly shrink if the phase changes minutely. However, dynamical systems can also experience significant changes due to small perturbations in parameters; the vortex rings can reconnect, nucleate or collapse into a point. Parameters that cause such striking outcomes are at the focal point of catastrophe theory - a branch of bifurcation theory that studies degenerate critical points of a potential function. We present theoretical study of topological configurations of optical vortex rings in elliptic Gaussian beams, which change dramatically at specific beam parameters. We identify two types of catastrophes, cusp and butterfly, near which very small changes of elliptic deformations lead to complex topological transformations of vortex rings.

title: New Developments in Diagrammatic Monte Carlo for Interacting Lattice Fermions: Efficient Algorithms and Applications
comment: PhD thesis with extended derivations and additional technical details beyond those presented in the corresponding manuscripts
summary:
This thesis develops diagrammatic methods for thermodynamic and subsystem quantities of interacting lattice fermions, providing reference calculations for quantum simulators and many-body approximations. I formulate an inverse-flavour expansion about a self-consistent Hartree saddle, enumerate non-Gaussian diagrams, and use a discrete Lehmann representation to integrate selected internal vertices analytically. Density results cover 31 state points of the six-flavour Hubbard model on a $70\times70$ lattice at $T/t=0.15$.
  I generalize combinatorial summation to flavour-dependent propagators and expansion shifts. CoS++ combines partial contractions to obtain connected sums for interaction subsets. A determinant-polynomial sieve evaluates the same sums through local coefficient filters; at ninth order it is 24--25 times faster than the specified CoS baselines in three-flavour dense-random-matrix benchmarks. Thermodynamic applications include a 2048-site honeycomb lattice and a three-flavour square lattice with 1024 sites.
  For the second Renyi entropy, I derive a fermionic replica path integral and a stable evaluation of its two-time Green functions. The connected-determinant calculation reaches tenth order on a $3\times3$ cluster and ninth order on larger lattices. On $50\times50$ sites at $(U/t,μ/t,βt)=(3,1,8)$, the ninth-order continuation at shift $α=1.3$ gives $S_2/N_s=0.06695$ with propagated Monte Carlo uncertainty $3.0\times10^{-5}$. Comparing two expansion shifts at their respective retained orders gives an endpoint difference of $2.6\times10^{-4}$.

title: Free-vortex-wake dynamics of airborne wind energy kites in crosswind flight
summary: The wake of an airborne wind energy kite is shaped by its crosswind path and, for on-board generation, by the slipstreams of its rotors, and in farms it reaches downstream units. It is computed here by a vortex step method with a time-marching free vortex wake, implemented by the authors in their open-source code OpenFAWE with a lumped-mass tether, actuator-disc rotors releasing vortex rings and several kites. It reproduces an independent vortex step code to 10^-9 on the rigid-wing Makani M600 and within 0.3% in lift and 0.9% in drag on the TU Delft V3 leading-edge inflatable kite, matching its Reynolds-averaged Navier-Stokes lift within 3.1%. For fixed kites the lift deficit of a finite wake is the far field of its starting vortex, which fixes the wake length before a run, and the vortex core must stay below the narrowest panel width. With these settings the helical tip-vortex pair of the M600 on its loop lowers its lift by about 0.5% from 5 to 13 m/s. Free rotor rings do not converge with the time step, whereas an undeformed slipstream tube converges once its rings are refined at the wing and raises the lift by 1.9%. A slipstream deflected by the wing lowers it by 3.5%, so the treatment near the wing sets the sign of the rotor effect. A second unit one loop diameter downstream loses 0.5% of its lift and 2.2% of its aerodynamic power, with or without rotors.

title: Surface-Illuminated Interdigitated Ge-on-Si Avalanche Photodiode With Separated Ge Absorption, Si Multiplication, and Lateral Field Engineering
comment: Submitted to IEEE Journal of Lightwave Technology; under review
summary: This work presents a surface-illuminated lateral Ge-on-Si interdigitated separate-absorption-charge-multiplication (SACM) avalanche photodiode for 1550-nm detection. The intrinsic-region spacing, P$^-$ charge-control width, and finger geometry are engineered to suppress high-field penetration toward the Ge/Si heterointerface and localize avalanche multiplication in Si. Simulations show that wider charge-control or intrinsic regions reduce fixed-bias dark current and shift avalanche onset to higher reverse bias. Among the tested structures, the intrinsic-region spacing/P$^-$ charge-control width of 0.5/0.15 $μ$m achieved a peak responsivity of 11.81 A/W at 1550 nm. At a -20 V applied voltage, it exhibited a multiplication gain of 3.796, a 3-dB bandwidth of 7.13 GHz, and a matched-bias gain-bandwidth product of 27.07 GHz. Optical-power-dependent measurements also show avalanche-gain compression consistent with space-charge screening. These results demonstrate effective lateral-field engineering for high-speed, surface-illuminated Ge-on-Si APDs.

title: AMOR: Adaptive Modal Operator Refinement for Operator Learning on Arbitrary Meshes and Irregular 3D Geometries
comment: 50 pages, 13 figures, 11 tables. Submitted to Computer Methods in Applied Mechanics and Engineering. Code: https://github.com/leonardvetter/AMOR; data: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18815516
summary: Parametric PDEs in science and engineering are often posed on irregular meshes with geometries that may contain holes or complex boundaries, yet popular operator-surrogate architectures such as the Fourier Neural Operator (FNO) rely on structured geometries for fast computational kernels. We introduce Adaptive Modal Operator Refinement (AMOR), which replaces FNO's Fourier-based spectral convolutions with reduced-basis blocks and supports both data-driven and prescribed input/output bases through a common encode/decode interface. AMOR thus applies unmodified to arbitrary meshes and, because its spectral parameterization has no tensor-product dependence on the spatial dimension, it scales favorably to three dimensions, where FNO's spectral weights grow as $m^3$ with the number of spectral modes $m$. We prove that AMOR is a universal approximator of continuous operators. On two-dimensional structured-grid benchmarks, AMOR is competitive with FNO overall and surpasses PCANet: it outperforms FNO on nonlinear diffusion and Helmholtz problems, while a static snapshot basis keeps it from matching FNO's accuracy on the time-dependent Kolmogorov flow problem. On three-dimensional problems it matches or exceeds FNO's accuracy at lower inference cost on linear elastostatics while trailing FNO on a turbulent lid-driven-cavity flow and scales favorably to problems demanding high capacity. On irregular meshes, where FNO is not directly applicable, AMOR reduces the relative $L^2$ error over the FNO extension Geo-FNO by $31\%$ (airfoil) and $42\%$ (elasticity). Finally, AMOR maintains strong performance across three physically distinct, experimentally motivated loading regimes on a topologically nontrivial three-dimensional aircraft-rib mesh, demonstrating its applicability to realistic engineering problems without modification.

title: Mode-2 solitary waves in continuous stratifications
summary: Computed herein are examples of mode-2 internal solitary waves to the Dubreil-Jacotin-Long (DJL) equation. These are localised, fully nonlinear waves in a continuously stratified, inviscid fluid under the Boussinesq and rigid-lid approximations. The equation is solved directly using finite differences on a periodic domain, enabling the computation of both generalised solitary waves, which possess oscillatory mode-1 tails, and embedded solitary waves, whose tails vanish. Two stratifications are considered. The first is a double pycnocline, generalising the three-layer system considered by Doak et al. (2022) by replacing each infinitesimal interface with a pycnocline of finite thickness. The second stratification, a surface mixed layer above an exponentially stratified layer, shows that embedded mode-2 solitary waves are not restricted to double-pycnocline stratifications. These are the first mode-2 solitary waves of the DJL equation computed for stratifications that are asymmetric about mid-depth.

title: Rubidium-Referenced Frequency-Doubled Pockels Laser with High-Speed Electro-Optic Tuning
summary: Narrow-linewidth lasers with rapid frequency control are essential for atomic physics and quantum technologies, yet combining these capabilities in chip-integrated sources at visible wavelengths remains challenging. Here we demonstrate a hybrid integrated InP/thin-film lithium niobate Pockels laser that emits at 780 nm through intracavity second-harmonic generation and supports gigahertz-bandwidth frequency tuning. A periodically poled lithium niobate waveguide is embedded in a laser cavity terminated by an extended distributed Bragg reflector, which provides electro-optically tunable feedback only at the 1560 nm fundamental wavelength. This design yields a singly resonant cavity that enhances frequency conversion while allowing the second-harmonic output to follow rapid tuning without resonance alignment. The laser achieves intrinsic linewidths of 2.7 kHz at 1560 nm and 9.0 kHz at 780 nm, with electro-optic tuning bandwidths beyond 1 GHz at both wavelengths. A mode-hop-free tuning range of 6.48 GHz at 780 nm enables direct spectroscopy of the rubidium D2 transition. Locking the second-harmonic output to this transition reduces the standard deviation of its frequency fluctuations from 135 MHz to 8 MHz and transfers the atomic frequency reference to the fundamental. These results establish integrated frequency-doubled Pockels lasers as compact, rapidly tunable sources that could simplify the optical architectures for future atomic and quantum photonic systems.

title: Recovering Non-Maxwellian Velocity Distribution Functions from Collective Thomson Scattering Spectra Using Generalized Basis Representations
comment: 16 pages, 10 figures. G. A. Baker and B. Klein contributed equally to this work. This article has been submitted to Physics of Plasmas. After it is published, it will be found at https://pubs.aip.org/aip/pop
summary: Thomson scattering (TS) is a key diagnostic for inferring plasma parameters from scattered power spectra, but its interpretation depends strongly on assumptions about the underlying velocity distribution functions (VDFs). Conventional analyses typically assume Maxwellian distributions, which can be invalid in high-energy-density and laboratory astrophysics plasmas where collisionless, multi-population dynamics produce non-thermal features. In such cases, Maxwellian models may reproduce observed spectra while yielding inaccurate or misleading plasma parameters. We present a generalized TS analysis framework that represents species-specific VDFs in flexible, physically motivated bases and so reconstructs complex, non-equilibrium distributions. To explore the resulting high-dimensional parameter space, we build the forward model from differentiable operations and optimize the VDF parameters by gradient descent. We apply the method to synthetic TS spectra generated from particle-in-cell simulations of a collisionless shock with interacting hydrogen and carbon populations. Immediately upstream of the shock, where the plasma is most non-thermal, the flexible bases cut the mean normalized ion VDF residual from 38.7% for a Maxwellian model to 20.3% and 20.5%, with correspondingly improved time-resolved plasma parameters. We also introduce a systematic method of uncertainty quantification that reveals degeneracies between ion species, highlighting the importance of both flexible VDF modeling and a statistical mapping of the solution space for this inherently ill-posed inversion problem.

title: diff-soup: GPU-native Differentiable Simulation and Inference for Large-scale Stiff Dynamical Systems
summary: Learning physical models from spatiotemporal data requires simulating systems of partial differential equations (PDEs) and differentiating through their solution. Upon spatial discretization, these models give rise to stiff dynamical systems that require repeatedly solving large, sparse linear systems. Traditional scientific computing frameworks are largely CPU-based and require problem-specific tuning to accelerate, scale, and differentiate. In this work, we introduce diff-soup, a differentiable, sparse-oriented, unified PDE suite for GPU-native simulation and inference of large, stiff dynamical systems. Built in JAX, diff-soup provides 1) a fully differentiable design for problems with sparse structure, 2) scaling to large problems through the NVIDIA cuDSS sparse direct solver with model and data multi-GPU parallelism, and 3) end-to-end PDE-constrained optimization, from classical statistical inference to embedded deep learning. On stiff PDE benchmarks, diff-soup outperforms established CPU- and GPU-based frameworks by one to two orders of magnitude in both forward solves and gradients. We demonstrate both a classical Bayesian inference workflow, identifying constitutive relationships, and a modern deep learning workflow, training a neural field for the catalyst activity of a three-dimensional packed bed reactor. We provide diff-soup as an open-source repository to facilitate research in computational science and engineering.

title: DSMC Study on Unsteadiness of Supersonic Flow Over a Cylinder
comment: 19 pages, 11 figures. Presented at the AIAA SciTech 2026 Forum, 12-16 January 2026, Orlando, FL. Published by AIAA, DOI: 10.2514/6.2026-2147. Copyright 2026 by the American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics, Inc. All rights reserved. Author version; reference list typos corrected
summary: Unsteady flow over a 30 $μ$m diameter cylinder at Mach 4 is investigated using Direct Simulation Monte Carlo across Reynolds numbers from 270 to 6750, spanning slip-flow to near-continuum regimes. Power Spectral Density analysis at discrete probe locations and Dynamic Mode Decomposition of flowfield snapshots independently characterize instabilities in both the stagnation and wake regions. In the stagnation region, a bow shock pulsation mode at 10-15 MHz frequency is identified across all cases despite a 24-fold variation in number density. In the wake, two distinct instabilities are observed. The canonical vortex shedding mode at Strouhal number St $\approx$ 0.2 dominates at lower Reynolds numbers. A second instability at St $\approx$ 0.5, consistent with previously reported slipline-driven oscillations in supersonic wakes, emerges at higher Reynolds numbers and progressively strengthens, becoming the dominant mode. In the studied Reynolds range, the wake transitions from no clear unsteadiness, to canonical vortex shedding at St $\approx$ 0.20, and reaching a regime where the St $\approx$ 0.5 mode becomes dominant, while also having a distinct independent bow shock pulsation possibly governed by its standoff distance.

title: Wavefunction-templated metamaterials
summary: Metamaterials, which store, guide and emit waves through their eigenmodes, have enabled the development of devices with unprecedented functionalities. Yet the spatial profiles of conventional metamaterials' eigenmodes are typically determined by their pre-determined structures (Hamiltonians). In this work, we introduce `wavefunction-templated metamaterials', a class of physically realizable metamaterials hosting diverse prescribed, spectrally isolated eigenstates. The resulting Hamiltonian geometries obey a boundary law, with the required nonlocality determined solely by single-contact boundary sites, independent of the state interior or lattice size. The sparse Hamiltonians are then Hermitianized, followed by spectral reshaping to open a protective gap around the target eigenstate. We validate our approach in discrete lattices and acoustic metamaterials. Although demonstrated in acoustics, the principle can be applied to thermal, electrical-circuit and photonic metamaterials.

title: A Comparison of Electric-Field Profile Reconstruction Methods based on the E-FISH Diagnostic
summary: Electric-field-induced second harmonic generation (EFISH) is a non-intrusive, non-resonant technique for measuring electric fields in moderate-to-atmospheric pressure plasmas. However, its nonlinear, path-integrated nature introduces measurement uncertainty, preventing a unique relationship between the measured signal and local electric field. One approach to overcome this limitation is to acquire spatial EFISH profiles and invert them to reconstruct the underlying electric-field distribution. Although several inversion methods have been employed, their reconstruction accuracy and overall performance have yet to be systematically evaluated. This study compares three methods: machine learning, linear inversion, and Abel inversion, using EFISH measurements from four electrode geometries with distinct electric-field distributions. Their performance is evaluated in terms of reconstruction accuracy, robustness to sparse data and noise, and ability to reconstruct asymmetric profiles. All three methods successfully reconstruct electric-field profiles, but exhibit distinct advantages and limitations. Machine learning provides high accuracy, computational speed, and noise resilience, but performs poorly on profiles that differ substantially from its training data, particularly asymmetric profiles. Linear inversion accommodates a broader range of field distributions but is sensitive to the initial profile. Abel inversion is limited to axisymmetric fields but performs well for horizontal field polarization. The complementary limitations of machine learning and linear inversion motivate a potential hybrid approach for reconstructing electric fields with unknown spatial distributions. Overall, this study identifies key trade-offs among the methods and provides guidance for selecting suitable reconstruction strategies under different measurement conditions.

title: Magnetic crystal generation with site-resolved magnetic moments via Gaussian-mixture retargeting and finite-budget yield prediction
comment: Main text: 28 pages, 8 figures; Supplementary Information: 31 pages, 2 figures (included)
summary: We introduce GMMag, a workflow for generating crystal structures together with their site-resolved magnetic moments, built on a conditional variational autoencoder with a graph neural network encoder and a transformer decoder. Gaussian-mixture sampling redirects generation towards selected chemical and magnetic targets without retraining. We systematically investigate how encoder and decoder design, the representation of magnetic-moment magnitudes and relative signs, and sampling choices affect reconstruction, generation quality and diversity. Because a higher screening pass rate does not necessarily yield more qualifying candidates with distinct chemical formulas absent from the reference dataset, we model how repeated generation of the same chemical formulas limits their accumulation and test the model in two separate ten-million-draw runs. As an application, the workflow identifies Nd-containing candidates with chemical formulas absent from the reference dataset, negative formation energies and high estimated saturation magnetization.

title: Local Metrics for Exact Streaming on Curvilinear Lattices: A Curvilinear D3Q27 Cumulant Lattice-Boltzmann Method
summary:
A three-dimensional curvilinear lattice-Boltzmann method is introduced for simulations on smoothly deformed grids while retaining exact one-to-one streaming on a uniform computational lattice. The coordinate transformation is represented locally through a metric-Gaussian equilibrium and a Christoffel-connection source in moment space. A dynamically reconstructed homogeneous-state perturbation streaming procedure preserves homogeneous physical states on warped meshes without interpolation in the advection step. The method is implemented on a D3Q27 lattice with a cumulant collision operator, while the geometric construction remains compatible with other local collision models.
  The formulation is assessed using two sets of tests. First, static non-orthogonal warped-cube cases validate the bulk curvilinear solver through a convected helical shear wave, the Taylor--Green vortex, and Arnold--Beltrami--Childress flow. These tests verify viscous decay, clean freestream preservation, vortex-breakdown dynamics, and the nonlinear inertial--pressure balance induced by geometric acceleration. Second, wall-bounded and moving-boundary demonstrations assess the boundary-compatible extension through warped plane Poiseuille flow, arbitrary Lagrangian--Eulerian (ALE) peristaltic pumping, and a two-way fluid--structure interaction (FSI) case with added-mass frequency shift. The results show that the proposed curvilinear LBM avoids interpolation-based transport, reduces geometry-locked numerical modes, preserves global mass and momentum to round-off accuracy in the tested warped periodic cases, and extends to wall-bounded ALE/FSI configurations with conservative treatment of mass and physically consistent momentum exchange.

title: Channel-Differentiated Topological Charge Flips and Formation of Janus Bound States in the Continuum in Single-Layer Photonic Lattices
summary: The topological charge of a bound state in the continuum (BIC) can flip when the BIC merges with other polarization singularities or, as recently shown, at band flips. Here, using a coupled-mode analysis, we derive an analytical expression for the topological charge of symmetry-protected BICs in one-dimensional single-layer photonic lattices. The expression captures both merging-induced and band-flip-induced charge flips. We find that, during a band flip, the topological charge of the BIC reverses with the formation of lines of circular polarization that cross at the $Γ$ point. In vertically symmetric lattices, each charge flip occurs simultaneously in the upward and downward radiation channels. Breaking vertical symmetry makes both kinds of charge flips channel-differentiated, creating a parameter interval in which the BIC carries opposite topological charges in the two channels and forms a Janus BIC. We show that Janus BICs also emerge in experimentally accessible one- and two-dimensional silicon-based photonic lattices. Our results link the topological charge of a BIC directly to the band structure and the channel-resolved radiation amplitudes and establish a basis for channel-selective control of polarization singularities.

title: Comparative analysis of tungsten armor and a liquid-lithium film as first walls for the HiPER laser-fusion chamber: thermal response, vapor shielding and helium transmission to the steel
comment: 24 pages main text + 39 pages supplementary material. Code: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23577155
summary: Tungsten armor and liquid-metal films, the usual sacrificial first walls of laser-fusion chambers, were modeled separately. Both go through one calculation for the three HiPER scenarios: NRL 154 MJ spectra scaled by yield, binned to keep each ion species' number and energy, a common deposition model, and a one-dimensional enthalpy solver with melting, evaporation and parameterized vapor shielding. In Demo (154 MJ, 6.5 m, 10 Hz), a 1 mm tungsten armor peaks 378 K below melting without neutron heating (275-319 K with it). A degraded near-surface conductivity can erase this margin, which also depends on the ion-spectra construction. The steel interface exceeds the 925 K limit, and the surface accumulates the 10^18-10^19 m^-2 helium fluences associated with the onset of surface modification within 10-98 shots (not a lifetime). A lithium film keeps the steel below 925 K from 44 um and below the 873 K compatibility limit from 56 um, more with partial renewal. Burn ions then implant helium; keeping the steel below 10^18 m^-2 for 10^6 shots needs 184 um, which binds in every scenario. The film evaporates 7.4x10^-4 kg m^-2 per shot (range 4.2-8.4x10^-4 kg m^-2, full renewal). Vapor shielding, with a nearly un-ionized vapor (Saha estimate), changes this by -21 % to +5 % for the Saha-supported stopping factor s = 1 and -34 % to +8 % across s = 1-2. Both walls are thermally viable in Prototype and marginal for tungsten in Demo. The deciding issues are tungsten damage evolution, lithium film survival and chamber clearing.

title: Spin-Orbit-Torque-Driven Recurrent Motion of Synthetic Antiferromagnetic Skyrmions for Magnetic Clocking
summary: Magnetic skyrmions in synthetic antiferromagnets have emerged as attractive information carriers for spintronic technologies due to their compensated topology, which mitigates the skyrmion Hall effect and facilitates reliable current-driven transport. Here we present a frequency-tunable magnetic clocking concept based on the recurring translational motion of SAF skyrmions and define the material conditions needed to realize it in a Pt/Co/Ru/Pt/Co multilayer. Using micromagnetic simulations, we investigate the combined effects of interfacial Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction and interlayer Ruderman-Kittel-Kasuya-Yosida exchange coupling, delineating the parameter space in which coupled Néel-type skyrmions with opposite topological charges form a stable, topologically compensated pair. Under spin-orbit torque excitation, the SAF skyrmions exhibit resilient longitudinal transport with minimal transverse deflection using periodic boundary conditions. Periodic boundary conditions serve as an idealized model for closed-loop racetrack geometries, facilitating the study of continuous transport cycles and long-range steady-state dynamics. The oscillation frequency is readily modified by the applied current density and material characteristics, offering a pathway to field-free nanoscale timing components. Moreover, the threshold-activated initiation of recurrent transport mimics tonic-spiking behavior, indicating possible use in neuromorphic signal generation. This work establishes SAF skyrmions as versatile building elements for future spintronic functional devices by integrating topological protection, controllable transport, and cyclic dynamics.

title: Wall modes in rotating penetrative internally heated convection
summary: Rotating internally heated convection has been studied almost exclusively in laterally periodic domains, which cannot support the sidewall-attached modes that appear for sufficient rotation rates in rotating Rayleigh--Bénard convection in containers. We conduct direct numerical simulations of internally heated convection with isothermal plates and an adiabatic sidewall in cylinders of aspect ratio $Γ= 1/2$, $1$, and $2$ at $\Ra = 10^8$ and $\Pran = 1$, comparing them with a doubly periodic layer. When rotation is strong enough to stabilise the flow in a doubly periodic layer at the same $R$ ($\Ek \lessapprox 2 \times 10^{-5}$), the cylinders continue transporting heat via a wall mode down to $\Ek = 5.62 \times 10^{-6}$. This mode consists of a wave attached to the sidewall, with a radial thickness of roughly $0.03$ layer depths independent of $Γ$, leaving a stationary interior. Although unstable stratification is confined to the upper half of the conductive state, the mode also penetrates the lower half while retaining stable mean stratification in the measured lower-layer interval. Its azimuthal wavenumber scales roughly with $Γ$, yielding a wall parallel wavelength on the order of the layer depth, and it drifts retrograde as a rigid wave slower in wider cylinders and at lower $\Ek$. Analogous to rotating Rayleigh--Bénard convection, the wall modes reported here extend the observed range of sustained convection relative to the periodic reference and may complicate experimental comparisons.

title: Study of Multilayer TiNx/Ti/TiNx Films Formed In Situ for High-Efficiency Integrated Microheaters
summary: A technology for the in situ formation of a three-layer TiN$_x$/Ti/TiN$_x$ functional material within a single vacuum cycle is presented, together with the results of investigations of its structural and electrophysical properties. The maximum critical power density reached approximately 140 MW/cm$^2$. Under continuous operation at 90% of the critical power, the structures remained operational for 24 h. The characteristics of microbridges without and with a protective SiO$_x$ layer were compared. The presence of the coating modifies the electrothermal operating regime of the structures and enables estimated temperatures of approximately 500-700 degrees Celsius to be reached.

title: Self-organized hybrid scenario mediated by fishbone modes in the EAST tokamak
summary: Self-organized hybrid scenario mediated by fishbone modes in the Experimental Advanced Superconducting Tokamak (EAST) is reported in this work. In this regime, internal transport barriers(ITBs) and a flat core safety factor profile were maintained simultaneously by fishbone modes. First,the drive of low-frequency flows by fishbone modes is clarified, which subsequently suppresses turbulence transport. Besides, fishbone-induced poloidally symmetric (m = 0) toroidal current sheets were first reported experimentally, which drive outward current redistribution that mitigates core current peaking. Together, these effects enable hybrid operation with stable ITBs and robust magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) stability, revealing a self-organized pathway for sustaining hybrid scenario for fusion reactors.

title: Effective Noise Thresholds for Reliable Quantum Approximation Optimisation Algorithm under Noisy Environment
summary: Variational quantum algorithms are leading candidates for practical utilisation on noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) processors, but accumulating noise bounds the usefulness of circuit depths. For the quantum approximate optimisation algorithm (QAOA), this trade-off has mostly been addressed by searching for the best depth for a given device. In this work, we consider the inverse question: how much noise each depth can tolerate. Using GPU-accelerated noisy QAOA simulations for MaxCut on three graph families with 6 to 18 vertices, depths up to 10 and three noise channels, we fit the approximation ratios with a generalised logistic surface. We propose the effective noise threshold as the inflection boundary of the logistic surfaces, a noise boundary separating reliable and unreliable QAOA approximation regimes. In general, the threshold decreases as depth rises, indicating that deeper circuits demand for stricter noise requirement for reliable approximation. Its best and worst values over depth divide the noise axis into three regions: every depth remains effective, depth must be chosen with care, or no depth induces effective optimisation. Assessing on the ibm_marrakesh processor, although modelled gate errors understate factual noise, the threshold modeling remains beneficial in informing qualitative depth-dependence structure and identifying dominating noise channel in noisy QAOA.

title: Learning the solution operator of standing waves with a Fourier neural operator
summary: The standing wave problem concerns the space-time periodic motion at the free surface of a two-dimensional, infinitely deep, irrotational flow of an incompressible inviscid fluid under gravity. Although spectrally accurate computations have revealed a rich array of nonlinear wave phenomena, repeatedly evaluating their evolution over large parameter spaces remains challenging, particularly when resolving fine-scale spatial oscillations. We employ a Fourier neural operator (FNO) architecture to learn the solution operator along a numerically computed one-parameter family of symmetric standing waves. Given a wave profile at an instant of rest and a normalized observation time, the learned operator predicts the fluid surface, the velocity potential and the dipole density at the surface at that time. In-distribution tests yield uniformly small relative errors within the training range. Two out-of-distribution experiments characterize extrapolation toward contrasting physical regimes. Toward the free-fall limit, errors concentrate near the sharpening crest, consistent with the spectral truncation in the FNO architecture. Toward the linear limit, absolute errors remain small whereas relative errors increase as the amplitude vanishes. A residual of the governing equations, evaluated independently of reference solutions, complements these tests and provides a diagnostic for exploratory predictions beyond the available data.

title: Optically gated transduction enables silicon electrical readout of mid-infrared light
summary: Silicon is the dominant platform for integrated photonics, yet its wide electronic bandgap of 1.1 eV fundamentally prevents efficient detection of mid-infrared (MIR) photons through direct valence band to conduction band excitation. Existing approaches therefore seek to enhance sub-bandgap absorption or introduce external infrared absorbers. Here we demonstrate a profoundly different detection strategy based on optically gated transduction, in which MIR photons modulate a pre-established excitation state rather than directly generating photocarriers. Our device integrates Nd3+-doped lanthanide nanoparticles with an inverse-designed Al/p-Si metasurface supporting dual resonances that simultaneously enhances optical gating in the near infrared and resonantly couples incident MIR radiation. The MIR illumination redistributes the Nd3+ emission pathways, producing an optical-state change that is converted into an electrical signal through a silicon Schottky junction. The device achieves room-temperature zero-bias detection at 6.8 um with a modulation responsivity of 103 uA/W and resolves combined gate and MIR inputs into three electrically distinguishable current states. Rather than extending silicon absorption into the infrared, this work establishes gated optical transduction as a route for reading MIR optical information on a silicon platform, opening opportunities for integrated infrared sensing, signal processing and programmable photonic systems.

title: Neutron-Lean D-3He Fusion by Asymmetric Enhancement of the Primary Reaction: A Spin-Polarized Non-Thermal Hot Tail
summary: This paper focuses on a modified fuel that combines the theory of spin-polarized fuel with non-thermal "hot-tail" reactions for D-T, D-3He, and D-D reactions. We find that this combination is particularly advantageous for the D-3He fuel in several respects. First, a large reactivity enhancement: one order of magnitude at 10 keV for a small hot tail (F = 0.1), rising to two orders of magnitude for a larger one (F = 0.6), with polarization adding a further factor of 1.5. Second, an ideal ignition energy far below the thermal value: 9.5 keV at F = 0.3 down to 3.2 keV at F = 0.5, which polarization reduces further to 3.8 keV and 1.3 keV, respectively. Third, the asymmetric enhancement between the primary reaction and the secondary reactions in the fuel opens the possibility of a neutron-lean reaction. Quantifying this with a neutrons-per-watt metric, we find that a thermal D-3He plasma at 10 keV is barely neutron-lean at all (90-95% of the D-T neutron rate per watt), whereas a hot tail of F = 0.1 reduces it by 4.7-7.7x and the polarized non-thermal fuel at its ignition point reaches 3.0-5.4% of the D-T value, with only 0.4-2.4% of the fusion power carried by neutrons. The range spans prompt removal versus complete in-situ burnup of the bred tritium. Applied to a 200 MW worked example anchored on the ARTEMIS D-3He reactor design, this is a first-wall neutron loading of 0.008-0.043 MW/m^2 against 1.45 MW/m^2 for D-T in the same chamber, extending the time to reach 20 dpa from about 1.5 full-power years to 27.

title: Reduced magnetohydrodynamics with electron inertia in pseudodipole coordinates
summary: We study the altitude-dependent structuring of field-aligned currents by driven Alfvén waves in an expanding auroral flux tube. The model uses the reduced magnetohydrodynamics (RMHD) long-thin ordering assumptions along with electron inertia. We derive a magnetic tension operator consistent with energy conservation in the expanding geometry. We compare uniform density with a prescribed profile containing a dense ionospheric end and a low-density upper region. The simulations produce localized current concentrations near the lower boundary and filamentary structures at greater heights. Broad structures remain visible in the magnetic and velocity stream functions while their perpendicular derivatives reveal finer magnetic field, velocity, and current structure. With the nonuniform density profile, the run with additional upper boundary reflection shows finer current structure and greater numerical dissipation. Spectral diagnostics show forward nonlinear energy transfer and altitude-dependent power-law-like intervals without a broad constant-flux range. The narrowest current concentrations span only a few grid cells, so their physical widths remain unresolved.

title: A regularized lattice Boltzmann model for the solid-liquid phase change
summary: In this study, a regularized lattice Boltzmann method is proposed for solid-liquid phase-change simulations. The governing total-enthalpy equation is solved within a regularized lattice Boltzmann (RLB) framework, which enables accurate tracking of the solid-liquid interface while effectively suppressing numerical diffusion. In addition, the multi-relaxation-time RLB (MRT-RLB) model with standard lattices is developed to solve the flow field. To enhance computational efficiency, an efficient multi-GPU (graphics processing unit) implementation based on CUDA C (Compute Unified Device Architecture) is developed, which is particularly suited for computationally intensive three-dimensional phase-change simulations. The proposed model is validated against a series of one-, two-, and three-dimensional benchmark problems. The results demonstrate that the present solver provides a robust, accurate, and efficient framework for simulating solid-liquid phase-change heat transfer.

title: High-Efficiency Graphene Oxide Moiré Lenses Enabled by Cyclic Self-Assembly and Laser Nanoprinting
summary: Compact optical systems with continuously tunable focal lengths are highly desirable for machine vision, biomedical imaging, and miniaturized cameras. Rotational Moiré lenses offer a planar approach to focal-length tuning, but metasurface-based implementations typically require complex nanofabrication processes that complicate large-area production. Here, we present a cyclic, mask-free fabrication strategy that combines layer-by-layer self-assembly of two-dimensional graphene oxide (GO) and poly(diallyldimethylammonium chloride) (PDDA) with femtosecond laser nanoprinting. Repeated GO-PDDA assembly and spatially selective ablation enable atomic-scale thickness control and the construction of precise multilevel phase profiles, reducing phase-quantization errors and improving focusing efficiency. The measured focusing efficiencies of individual GO lenses increase from 22.4% for two phase levels to 54.8% for six levels. Using this six-level modulation strategy, the fabricated GO Moiré lens achieves continuous focal-length tuning from approximately 10 to 90 mm. Full-colour imaging with magnifications ranging from 1X to 9X is experimentally demonstrated. These results establish a cyclic, mask-free fabrication strategy for efficient multilevel GO flat optics and demonstrate its potential for compact, reconfigurable imaging.

title: Elasticized magnetohydrostatics
summary: The modern approach to modeling equilibria in stellarators features two blind spots: lack of foundational agreement between theory and computation, and inability to reliably explore economically-attractive high-$β$ concepts. These blind spots originate at a technical level from lack of a useful existence theory for the partial differential equations believed to describe equilibria, and from the encumbrance of crude, inflexible models for the topology of the confining magnetic field. This Article proposes the first stellarator equilibrium model that rigorously guarantees existence of an equilibrium with any chosen magnetic topology. It completely separates determination of the magnetic topology from the equilibrium existence question, and thereby enables importing realistic tearing physics into equilibrium computations. The new model replaces the standard plasma potential energy functional with its ensemble average over rapid kinetic-scale fluctuations. Averaging ``elasticizes" the potential by energetically penalizing separation of field lines. The elasticized potential's super-linear dependence on plasma strain embodies a phenomenological model for profile stiffness, and plays an essential role in the existence theory.

title: DSMC Study of Hypersonic Boundary-Layer Unsteadiness Using Data-Driven Analysis
comment: 11 pages, 4 figures. Presented at the AIAA AVIATION 2026 Forum, 8-12 June 2026, San Diego, CA. Published by AIAA, DOI: 10.2514/6.2026-4737. Copyright 2026 by the American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics, Inc. All rights reserved. Author version; reference list typos corrected
summary: The prediction of transition remains challenging because the receptivity amplitude is usually prescribed rather than measured. This work uses Direct Simulation Monte Carlo (DSMC) to study an unforced Mach 6 nitrogen boundary layer over a 120 mm flat plate, with no imposed inlet wave, wall signal, modal shape, or disturbance spectrum. The retained unsteady field is the intrinsic finite-particle stochastic fluctuation field carried by the DSMC representation. Changing the DSMC particle count provides an independent numerical control parameter that sets a predictable finite-particle noise floor while preserving the time-averaged boundary-layer flow. Dynamic Mode Decomposition (DMD) is then applied to unforced DSMC snapshots. The DMD eigenvalues and spatial modes estimate the quantities that appear in the LST normal-mode description, including frequency, temporal growth or decay, wavenumber, wavelength, phase speed, mode location, and amplification envelope. LST is used after extraction to test whether the data-derived structures occupy the expected second-mode band. The results show that DSMC data can connect a measured finite-particle stochastic disturbance level to second-mode instability dynamics without imposed disturbance spectra.

title: Multiple-relaxation-time total enthalpy lattice Boltzmann model for liquid-vapor phase change
summary: In this paper, a multiple-relaxation-time (MRT) total enthalpy lattice Boltzmann (LB) model is proposed for liquid-vapor phase change. The pseudopotential LB method is employed to describe the liquid-vapor multiphase dynamics, while the thermal field is solved using an MRT LB formulation with total enthalpy as the evolution variable, thereby incorporating sensible and latent heat into a unified framework. A latent heat expression based on the equation of state (EOS) is further derived to provide a thermodynamic reference for its specification. Multiscale analysis demonstrates that the proposed model recovers the target macroscopic energy equation without introducing the nonlinear thermodynamic source term commonly required in temperature-based formulations, thereby avoiding the explicit evaluation of $\nabla\cdot\mathbf{u}$. The model is validated through free droplet evaporation, droplet evaporation on a heated surface, and bubble growth and departure during boiling, showing good agreement with published results. Simulations with different prescribed latent heats are further conducted in all three cases, demonstrating that the latent heat can be independently specified according to the physical conditions considered without altering the equation of state.

title: Multi-day single-cell magnetic imaging of living cancer cells using Quantum Cell Monitoring
summary: Live-cell imaging of cellular and tissue samples relies predominantly on optical modalities, such as fluorescence, confocal, and multiphoton microscopy, in which cellular information is encoded in emitted photons. Photons scatter and attenuate in biological samples, restricting depth resolution, while the excitation light required to produce them induces photodamage that perturbs the very biology under observation. Magnetic fields, by contrast, traverse biological samples without attenuation at cellular length scales, but the imaging modality that extracts the encoded information, magnetic resonance imaging, cannot resolve individual cells. Here we present Quantum Cell Monitoring (QCM), a widefield nitrogen-vacancy magnetometry platform that encodes single-cell information in stray magnetic fields rather than emitted photons and reads it out at subcellular resolution. Integrated with a specialized live-cell incubator, QCM tracks magnetically labeled living cancer for up to 72 h through their individual magnetic field signatures. It captures single-cell mitosis and morphological remodeling, as well as cell cluster formation, splitting, and migration even within dense regions where brightfield contrast collapses. By shifting the carrier of single-cell information from propagating optical photons to static magnetic stray fields, QCM decouples cell from cellular optical accessibility and auto-fluorescence, enabling sustained live-cell observation in regimes inaccessible to optical microscopy.

title: A generative foundation model for 2D magnetized plasma turbulence
summary: We present a proof-of-principle study demonstrating a conditional generative foundation model for self-organizing magnetized plasma turbulence. Built on a multichannel flow-matching framework with a spectral decomposition strategy, the model is trained on direct numerical simulations of 2D modified Hasegawa-Wakatani (MHW) turbulence across the hydrodynamic to adiabatic parameter range. Without retraining, this \textit{single} model successfully performs three distinct downstream tasks: (i) unconditional generation of statistically faithful quasi-steady-state snapshots that recover the directional energy spectra and amplitude statistics, from which statistical transport quantities, including turbulent flux and effective diffusivity, alongside their uncertainties, are inferred directly; (ii) super-resolution from $4\times$ and $8\times$ downsampled observations to reconstruct fine-scale turbulence and large-scale zonal structures; and (iii) full-field inpainting from sparse spatial observations covering as little as $\sim 10\%$ of the domain. The generated fields faithfully reproduce regime-dependent turbulence vs. zonal-flow states and energy partitioning. Under extreme sparsity the long-correlation zonal flows are pinned by only a handful of observations, while the residual uncertainty concentrates in the small-scale turbulent fluctuations. These results establish flow-matching generative models as powerful, unified surrogates for state generation, statistical inference, and sparse-data reconstruction, providing a scalable baseline for 3D plasma turbulence and experimental applications.

title: Rotation-driven suppression and re-emergence of unsteady flow past a circular cylinder
summary: The flow past a rotating cylinder undergoes substantial changes in its wake dynamics and aerodynamic response with increasing rotation rate. This study investigates these changes in two-dimensional compressible flow at \(Re_\infty=3800\) and \(M_\infty=0.1\), with the rotation rate systematically varied over \(0.1\leqΩ\leq10\) using 130 high-fidelity simulations. At low rotation rates, conventional periodic vortex shedding is progressively suppressed with increasing rotation. A narrow transition regime around \(Ω=2.2-2.8\) is identified, where sustained oscillations evolve into intermittent fluctuations before reaching a nearly quiescent state. At higher rotation rates, unsteadiness re-emerges with distinctly intermittent and multiscale characteristics, demonstrating that this instability is fundamentally different from conventional Kármán shedding. The surface pressure and streamwise skin-friction distributions reveal substantial redistribution of aerodynamic loading with rotation, characterized by increasingly intense suction and significant modification of the near-wall shear field. The maximum lift increases systematically with rotation, reflecting the strengthening Magnus-Robins effect, whereas drag exhibits a non-monotonic response with enhanced variability at high rotation rates. Despite the low free-stream Mach number, rotational acceleration produces local Mach numbers approaching 0.5, indicating appreciable compressibility effects in the near-cylinder region. Vorticity-based proper orthogonal decomposition further reveals a transition from wake-dominated coherent structures at low rotation to strongly wrapped, rotation-dominated structures at high rotation. These results establish a direct connection between rotational forcing, surface loading, compressibility, and the suppression and subsequent re-emergence of flow unsteadiness.

title: Ultrafast light-electron modulation for free-electron quantum optics: fundamentals and applications
summary: Coherent optical modulation of free-electron wavepackets offers a route to ultrafast beam steering, energy exchange, temporal compression, and quantum-state shaping. Recent advances in photon-induced near-field electron microscopy (PINEM), ultrafast Kapitza-Dirac effect (KDE) and dielectric laser acceleration (DLA) have demonstrated strong light-electron coupling, but longitudinal energy modulation, transverse momentum transfer, and wavepacket-dependent diffraction are still commonly described with separate models. Here, we develop a unified Light-Electron Modulation (LEM) framework that treats optical near fields as programmable phase modulators for free-electron wavepackets.
